title: Base change of a filtered colimit of algebras, elementwise
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ a filtered category whose objects and morphisms lie in the same universe as the underlying sets of the stage algebras and $i\mapsto A_i$ a functor from $I$ to the category of commutative $R$-algebras, with transition maps $A(u):A_i\to A_j$ for $u:i\to j$, colimit $A=\varinjlim_IA_i$ in that category [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] and coprojections $\iota_i:A_i\to A$. Let $N$ be an $R$-module, and put $\gamma_i=\iota_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_N:A_i\otimes_RN\to A\otimes_RN$ and $\gamma_u=A(u)\otimes\mathrm{id}_N:A_i\otimes_RN\to A_j\otimes_RN$. Then (1) every element of $A\otimes_RN$ is $\gamma_i(t)$ for some $i\in I$ and some $t\in A_i\otimes_RN$; (2) if $t\in A_i\otimes_RN$ satisfies $\gamma_i(t)=0$, then $\gamma_u(t)=0$ for some morphism $u:i\to j$ of $I$. (Equivalently, $A\otimes_RN$ with the maps $\gamma_i$ is a colimit of the diagram $i\mapsto A_i\otimes_RN$ of $R$-modules.) When $N$ is a commutative $R$-algebra, the $\gamma_i$ and $\gamma_u$ are ring homomorphisms.

proof.text: *Step 1 ($A$ is the colimit of the $A_i$ as $R$-modules).* By [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-algebras-underlying-module], applied to $R$, the small filtered category $I$ and the diagram $i\mapsto A_i$ of commutative $R$-algebras with its colimit $(A,(\iota_i))$, the $R$-module $A$ with the $R$-linear maps $\iota_i$ is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] of the diagram of $R$-modules $i\mapsto A_i$ with transition maps $A(u)$.

proof.text: Step 2 (tensor colimit universal property). Use the existing Lean theorem CommAlgCat.filteredColimit_tensorProduct_universal, which realizes the tensor-Hom argument of Tag 00DD: curry a compatible family of maps into Hom_R(N,M), descend it by CommAlgCat.filtered_colimit_algebras_underlying_module, and uncurry with TensorProduct.lift; uniqueness follows by TensorProduct.curry_injective. Form the functor G : I to ModuleCat R with objects A_i tensor_R N and maps LinearMap.rTensor N (F.map u).hom.toLinearMap. Its identity and composition laws are checked on pure tensors. Form its cocone c with point A tensor_R N and the stated coprojections; its naturality follows on pure tensors from colimit.w F u. Apply IsColimit.ofExistsUnique to the universal theorem to obtain hc : IsColimit c. This proves the parenthetical universal clause and supplies the colimit needed by step 3.

Step 3 (representatives and eventual zero). Apply the Mathlib realization of lem-weil-pbc-filtered-colimit-modules-elementwise to G and hc. To accommodate independent universes uR, uI and uN, put G in ModuleCat.{max uI uN} R, and show its forgetful functor preserves this colimit by composing forget₂ to AddCommGrpCat with forget AddCommGrpCat. ModuleCat.Colimits supplies preservation of colimits by the first functor. AddCommGrpCat.FilteredColimits supplies preservation by the second, resized from max uI uN to uI using preservesFilteredColimitsOfSize_shrink. Concrete.isColimit_exists_rep G hc yields every tensor representative. For a tensor t at i with zero image, rewrite its image as equal to the image of 0 at i, and apply Concrete.isColimit_exists_of_rep_eq G hc t 0. This gives an object j and arrows u,v : i to j with G.map u t = G.map v 0. Since linear maps send zero to zero, u is the required eventual-vanishing morphism. No new lemma or unproved dependency is introduced.

proof.text: *Step 4 (the ring structure when $N$ is an algebra).* Let $N$ be a commutative $R$-algebra. Each $\iota_i:A_i\to A$ and each $A(u):A_i\to A_j$ is a homomorphism of commutative $R$-algebras (they are morphisms of the category of commutative $R$-algebras). By [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-map-ring-hom] applied to $f=\iota_i$, resp. $f=A(u)$, the maps $\gamma_i=\iota_i\otimes\mathrm{id}_N$ and $\gamma_u=A(u)\otimes\mathrm{id}_N$ are homomorphisms of $R$-algebras, in particular ring homomorphisms.

old_proof.text: *Step 2 (tensoring with $N$; the 'equivalently' form).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-commutes-with-colimits] to the ring $R$, the small category $I$, the diagram of $R$-modules $i\mapsto A_i$ (transition maps $A(u)$) with the colimit $(A,(\iota_i))$ of step 1, and the $R$-module $N$. Its part (1) says that every element of $A\otimes_RN$ is $\gamma_i(t)$ for some $i\in I$ and $t\in A_i\otimes_RN$: this is (1). Its 'in particular' says that for $t\in A_i\otimes_RN$ with $\gamma_i(t)=0$ there is a morphism $u:i\to j$ of $I$ with $\gamma_u(t)=0$ (the transition map along $u$ being $\gamma_u$): this is (2).
